issues.legal_issue: Refusing to withdraw land from acquisition while granting withdrawal to similarly situated owners in the same acquisition proceedings is discriminatory when the different treatment has no valid basis.
material_facts: The owners sought withdrawal of their land from acquisition after the State had released land belonging to numerous other owners under the same acquisition proceedings and for the same public purpose.
Some of the other owners had vacant plots, and some had not challenged the acquisition; others had challenged it but their requests for release had not been recommended by the inspection committee.

Before the relevant later policy was adopted, the State had no uniform policy governing withdrawal, and that later policy had not been applied to the owners whose land was released in the same acquisition proceedings.
The State rejected the owners’ representations by relying on the later policy and did not allege that the comparable releases were unlawful, mistaken, fraudulent, or contrary to public interest.
The Court directed that land forming part of roads, common sites, or public utility areas would not be considered for release.
issues.conclusion: The State’s rejection of the representations was discriminatory and unlawful. The rejection order was set aside, and the State was directed to issue orders concerning the owners’ land on the same terms and in the same manner as the comparable releases, excluding portions forming part of roads, common sites, or public utility areas.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 requires fairness, consistency, and non-arbitrariness in State action, including discretionary decisions concerning withdrawal from acquisition. Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 empowers the Government to withdraw from acquisition before possession is taken and prescribes no particular procedure for doing so. A person has no right to repeat an unlawful benefit granted to someone else, but where the State has lawfully exercised its withdrawal power for similarly situated owners in the same acquisition, it must treat other similarly situated owners consistently and may not create artificial distinctions without a valid basis. The Court applied International Trading Co. v. Union of India (2003) 5 SCC 437 on reasoned and non-arbitrary State action; Sube Singh v. State of Haryana (2001) 7 SCC 545 on unreasonable classification; and the principles against negative equality discussed in Secretary, Jaipur Development Authority v. Daulat Mal Jain (2003) 5 SCC 437, Jalandhar Improvement Trust v. Sampuran Singh (1999) 3 SCC 494, Anand Buttons Ltd. v. State of Haryana (2005) 9 SCC 164, and Vishal Properties (P) Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2007) 11 SCC 172. Ved Prakash v. Ministry of Industry (2005) 9 SCC 164 was also considered concerning the State’s consideration of representations for withdrawal.

rule.if: appeal_from_rejection_of_withdrawal_representation and same_acquisition_and_public_purpose and comparable_owners_received_withdrawal and state_relied_on_standard_not_used_for_comparators and no_claim_comparator_releases_were_unlawful and requested_land_not_in_public_utility_area

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_withdrawal_repr: The proceeding challenges the State’s rejection of a landowner’s request to withdraw land from acquisition.
predicates.same_acquisition_and_public_purpose: The landowner’s land and the comparator owners’ land were acquired in the same proceedings for the same public purpose.
predicates.comparable_owners_received_withdrawal: The State withdrew comparable owners’ land from acquisition, including land with similar circumstances.
predicates.state_relied_on_standard_not_used_for_co: The State rejected the landowner’s request using a decision-making standard that it had not applied when releasing the comparator owners’ land.
predicates.no_claim_comparator_releases_were_unlawf: The State did not claim that the comparator owners’ releases were unlawful, mistaken, fraudulent, or contrary to public interest.
predicates.requested_land_not_in_public_utility_are: The land for which equal withdrawal treatment is sought does not form part of a road, common site, or public utility area.

issues.definition: When a landowner challenges the rejection of a withdrawal request, the land was acquired alongside comparable owners’ land for the same purpose, those owners received withdrawal, and the State used a different standard without alleging unlawful comparator releases, the State must provide the same withdrawal treatment for land outside public utility areas.
